title: Microsoft Teams: manage Microsoft 365 certified apps through org-wide third-party app settings
summary: The briefing overstates the bulk third-party app switch: it does not enable every app, because individually configured and blocked apps are exempt. The administrative paths, PowerShell call and reported rollout discrepancy are supported, but the bulk-control advice needs that qualification.

claims.claim: The Teams roadmap item enables administrators to manage Microsoft 365 certified SaaS apps through org-wide third-party app settings.
claims.quote: This feature allows Microsoft 365 administrators to enable Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps.

claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators can choose to allow a subset of applications.
claims.quote: Admins can choose to allow a subset of applications that have already been verified against industry security and compliance standards.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes those applications as already verified against industry security and compliance standards.
claims.quote: applications that have already been verified against industry security and compliance standards

claims.claim: The roadmap describes maintaining governance and reducing approval overhead.
claims.quote: This ensures organizations can confidently adopt apps while maintaining governance and reducing approval overhead.

claims.claim: The included model uses the product-level Teams licence requirement for users of Teams apps.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.claim: The Manage apps page requires the Teams Administrator role and recommends a lower-privilege role over higher-privilege alternatives.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams streamlined Microsoft 365 certified app management licensing price meter org-wide settings; opened manage-apps and user-access. Manage apps names the Teams Administrator role but no separate licence for these settings or views.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: Searched: Teams streamlined Microsoft 365 certified app management licensing price meter org-wide settings; opened manage-apps, app-centric-management, uam-tac-mac, user-access and purchase-third-party-apps. No licence specific to this management change was documented.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter or price specific to this management feature is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams streamlined Microsoft 365 certified app management licensing price meter org-wide settings; opened manage-apps, user-access and purchase-third-party-apps. No management-feature meter or price was found; paid app subscriptions are separately documented.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The bulk control is in Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Per-app allow or block is in Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and notes
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> to change per-app state.
claims.quote: This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app. Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls notes; Open questions
claims.claim: No PowerShell or Microsoft Graph setting for this org-wide Third-party apps control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide Third-party apps control PowerShell; "org-wide" "third-party" "PowerShell" app settings; "teamsAppSettings" "beta" third party. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management, Update-M365TeamsApp, teamsAppSettings v1.0/beta and Graph beta PowerShell search excerpts.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: After app-centric migration, a single third-party control manages bulk availability of new and existing apps.
claims.quote: Post app centric management migration, these are unified into a single control that governs bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The org-wide control does not override app-level configurations.
claims.quote: This control doesn't override app-level configurations. Your change to the org-wide app setting applies only to those apps for which you didn't change the availability.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Turning on the bulk control makes all new and existing third-party apps available, including all uncertified apps.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to: All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you. All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually. Any blocked apps.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket all-app statements with: 'The Third-party apps control changes the default availability of new apps and existing apps whose availability you have not individually configured; it is not limited to certified apps. Individually saved availability settings and blocked apps are exempt.' In At rollout, replace 'unless you intend to open all third-party apps' with 'unless you intend to enable third-party apps governed by the org-wide default'. Keep the app-centric-management citation.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Apps to consider allowing tile counts certified and publisher-attested apps, identifying their certification category.
claims.quote: The Teams admin center now includes Apps to consider allowing tile on the Manage apps page. This tile displays counts of Microsoft 365 certified and publisher-attested agents and apps, helping admins quickly identify trusted agents and apps.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Each app details page has a Security and Compliance tab displaying certification information.
claims.quote: A new Security and Compliance tab on each app’s details page displays its certification status, publisher attestation, and key security attributes etc.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document a certified-only option inside the Third-party apps control.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams Microsoft 365 certified apps org-wide settings certified only subset applications control. Opened manage-apps, app-centric-management and overview-of-app-certification; they document certification filtering and per-app management, not a certified-only bulk setting.

claims.claim: Certification involves developer-provided assessment information and audits against industry frameworks.
claims.quote: Developers provide answers to a questionnaire as part of their Teams app's security and compliance information for Publisher Attestation and for Microsoft 365 certification. Developers submit the comprehensive details as part of the audits done during certification.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An app's details page links its privacy policy, where the developer describes data use.
claims.quote: In the terms of use and privacy policy of any agent or app, the app developer discloses what data their agent or app uses and how it handles the data. This information is available on app developer's website and you can access the URLs in the app details page in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Consent to app permissions is distinct from allowing the app, and permissions still need review.
claims.quote: Once you decide to approve the use of an app, ensure that the app adoption is smooth for the users. A crucial part of the process is granting consent to the permissions that an app needs to work.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-consent-app-permissions to sources for the separate consent and permissions-review claim.

claims.claim: Only a Global admin can give final consent to unify a modified tenant in the documented scenarios.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.claim: Teams or Global admins can prepare unified-management changes through the Review summary page.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Saved org-wide settings take effect after a few hours.
claims.quote: Select Save. The settings take effect after a few hours.

claims.claim: After unification, availability-related changes in either admin centre synchronize to the other.
claims.quote: After unification, changes made to the app status, org-wide settings, and user assignment in either admin center are synchronized in the other.

claims.claim: Automatic app-centric migration started in April 2025, and the single bulk-control form is post-migration.
claims.quote: Starting from April 2025, your tenant is automatically migrated to app centric management. After migrating to app-centric management, a single control now manages bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps.

claims.claim: Administrators can view and manage only apps deployed in their tenant's release channel.
claims.quote: You can only view and manage agents and apps that are deployed in the same release channel as your tenant is.

claims.claim: Learn says third-party apps are blocked by default in GCC, GCC High and DoD deployments.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.claim: App-centric availability choices are Everyone, Specific users or groups, and No one.
claims.quote: Everyone: Available to all org users, new users, and guests. Specific users or groups: Only the users and groups that you select can use the app. No one: Not available to any user.

claims.claim: Administrators can export the app catalogue as CSV from the Manage apps page.
claims.quote: Export agent and app catalog as CSV. As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center. It can help you to coordinate with admin and security teams to evaluate agents and apps, verify availability, verify status, and more.

claims.claim: Users can request unavailable apps, and administrators receive notifications.
claims.quote: From within the Teams client, your users can request you to allow the agents and apps that aren't available for them. You receive notifications and can allow it.

claims.claim: Microsoft promises at least 60 days' advance notice for the future Phase 3 timeline.
claims.quote: We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.claim: The management change itself has no documented autonomous behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Microsoft 365 certified app management autonomous actions permissions consent allow app. Read manage-apps, uam-tac-mac, overview-of-app-certification and app-permissions search excerpts. No autonomous mechanism for the management change was found; apps' own actions are separate.

claims.claim: Learn says both org-wide and app-level settings must allow an app, while either can block it.
claims.quote: To allow an agent or app, you must do all of the following settings. To block an agent or app, use any one of the following settings: Org-wide app settings; App centric managemen.
claims.fix: Replace this paragraph with: 'The Manage apps page says both org-wide and user-level availability settings must allow an app. The app-centric management page qualifies this: org-wide defaults do not apply to individually saved app availability or blocked apps.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-apps and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management.

claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to review controls that have no corresponding table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'export the app catalogue as CSV', 'Review the Apps to consider allowing tile and the Security and Compliance tab', 'Check each app's availability', 'Check user requests'. Table rows: bulk availability and per-app allow/block only.
claims.fix: The checklist's CSV export, certification/compliance review, app-centric Everyone/Specific users or groups/No one availability review, and user-request review have no corresponding controls-table rows. Remove those checklist bullets to reconcile the checklist with the existing table; do not add rows in this correction.

claims.claim: The roadmap record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The PowerShell reference's example text describes -IsBlocked $true as unblocking.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true. Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Some third-party Teams apps require paid SaaS subscriptions available through AppSource or Manage apps.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers. A license is available for purchase from AppSource and in the Microsoft Teams admin center.

claims.claim: App permission policies are deprecated for tenants migrated to app-centric management.
claims.quote: Use agent and app assignment through app centric management to define user access for agents and apps. The previous App permission policies is deprecated.

claims.claim: The cited Graph teamsAppSettings resource lists two configurable properties unrelated to the bulk third-party control.
claims.quote: allowUserRequestsForAppAccess: Indicates whether users are allowed to request access to the unavailable Teams apps. isUserPersonalScopeResourceSpecificConsentEnabled: Indicates whether resource-specific consent for personal scope in Teams apps is enabled for the tenant.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence, meter or price.
claims.quote: This feature allows Microsoft 365 administrators to enable Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps.

claims.claim: Users of available apps can share data with them.
claims.quote: When you add the app to Teams, it gains access to some basic capabilities that might include access to basic information. When you grant consent, the app receives access to some data of user and organization or both, based on app permissions that it requested consent for.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-permissions to sources for the app data-access premise.
